solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink tea and sherry regularly

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word in front, at evenly spaced intervals

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of sherry

explanation.surface: Someone describes their habit of drinking tea and sherry on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken straight after another, typically a beer following a shot of spirits.

clue.text: Bird of paradise appearing in earliest part of day?

parts.note: an hour is one division of a day
I is the Roman numeral one, the first in sequence

explanation.surface: A beautiful bird is seen at dawn, the earliest part of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: hour one, the first hour of the day. 'Bird' is British slang for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is one of the beautiful maidens said to await the faithful in the Islamic paradise, so a woman of paradise.

clue.text: Less than average gent using public transport upset an unexperienced driver

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Mr is the title for a gentleman
someone using public transport is on a bus
the indefinite article in its short form
L is the learner plate on a novice driver's car

explanation.surface: A man taking the bus is annoyed by a learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Subnormal describes something falling below the usual or expected standard, beneath the norm.

clue.text: Rebellious conflict has troubled old kings

indicators.note: a rebellious thing turns against its order, so the word for conflict is read backwards

parts.note: to jar is to clash or conflict

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An uprising has disturbed the reign of ancient monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rajahs were Indian princes or rulers, a title associated with the historical era of Indian kingdoms.

clue.text: Give new look to flag, dropping central element

indicators.note: dropping the central element means the middle letter of the flag's name is removed

parts.note: the Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships

explanation.surface: A flag is being given a makeover by removing its central emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: RED ENSIGN has nine letters, and its fifth, N, is the one dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign something is to plan its appearance or structure afresh, changing how it looks.

clue.text: Visible evidence of past civilisation is yet to be discovered

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: ruins of an ancient culture that people can go and look at
second meaning: the everyday phrase for an outcome still unknown

explanation.surface: An archaeologist muses that the traces of an ancient civilisation have still not been found.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition takes the idiom word by word: remains that can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says an outcome is still uncertain and will become known later, while archaeological ruins are literally relics on view.

clue.text: Terminates recent court action

parts.note: to drop a plan or case is to end it
hot news is fresh, very recent

explanation.surface: Someone ends a recent lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' suggests a lawsuit, but the court is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shot is a softly played stroke in tennis or squash that falls just over the net, a move on court.

clue.text: Spread out and have fun after end of class

indicators.note: after places the piece for having fun behind the letter taken from class
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of class
to play is to have fun

explanation.surface: When lessons finish, the pupils scatter and enjoy themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To splay is to extend or open out wide, as when fingers or legs are spread apart.

clue.text: Infantryman rereading novel

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A foot soldier is going back over a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book being reread, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier of a grenadier regiment, historically a foot soldier who threw grenades.

clue.text: Blather from firm's ultimate high-fliers, first heading off

indicators.note: the first of the pair loses its heading, meaning its opening letter is removed
ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the firm's name is kept

parts.note: the last letter of firm
jumbos are jumbo jets, two of them here for the plural

explanation.surface: Nonsense spouted by a company's top executives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-fliers' suggests successful executives, but here it means two jumbo jets, the first losing its J.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbo-jumbo is meaningless or obscure talk, jargon or gibberish that sounds impressive but says nothing.

clue.text: Lascivious look of Lothario lacking companion

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letters for the companion are taken away

parts.note: a Lothario is a seducer of women, a lecher
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A womaniser on his own gives a lustful glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, suggestive or lustful sidelong glance at someone.

clue.text: One filling ruined his pork pies

indicators.note: something filling goes inside, so the letter for one is placed within the rest
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the following words are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cook complains that a filling has spoiled his pork pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Piroshki are small Russian baked or fried buns stuffed with meat, cabbage or other savoury fillings.

clue.text: Revolutionary workplace of broadcaster with large rating

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television company
L is the abbreviation for large
a rating is an ordinary sailor; AB is able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A TV channel's innovative office is famed for its big viewing figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests groundbreaking, but it means revolving round the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylab was the American space station of the 1970s, where astronauts worked while circling the planet in orbit.

clue.text: Junk mail disheartened sysop in the morning

indicators.note: losing its heart means the inner letters go, leaving just the outside pair

parts.note: the first and last letters of sysop
a.m. marks the hours before noon

explanation.surface: A system operator is dismayed to find unwanted email waiting first thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the name for unsolicited bulk electronic messages, usually advertising, flooding an inbox.

clue.text: Parking space that's been much used

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something that has been much used', a noun

parts.note: P is the sign for a car park
latitude is room or freedom to move

explanation.surface: A car parking bay has seen a great deal of use.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase meaning something worn out by repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a remark repeated so often that it has become stale and meaningless, an overworked saying.

clue.text: Kit currently adopted by Spain's premier clubs, perhaps

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the word for currently goes inside the other letters

parts.note: clubs are one suit in a deck of cards; perhaps signals an example
now means at present

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of Spain is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Spain

explanation.surface: A sports report on the strip now worn by Spain's top football clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit' and 'clubs' point to football, but clubs is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowsuit is a one-piece insulated outfit worn in cold weather, a set of clothing or kit.

clue.text: Polluted sea's vital waters

indicators.note: polluted means contaminated or spoiled, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A warning that contaminated sea water is harming vital marine life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waters' looks like a noun for the sea, but it is a verb: the mouth waters.
explanation.definitionFit: When the mouth waters at the sight of food, it produces spittle, which is exactly what salivating means.

clue.text: Bill feeding duck and lark

indicators.note: feeding puts one thing into another, so the bill goes inside the word for duck

parts.note: to duck something is to dodge or evade it
a bill is a poster, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A man called Bill gives food to a duck and a lark, two birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck and lark are not birds here: duck is a verb and lark means a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of mischievous fun, and an escapade is an adventurous or daring prank.

clue.text: Ring first over satellite

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
1st, with the digit read as the letter I
O is the abbreviation for an over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone first about a satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large moons of Jupiter, a natural satellite of that planet.

clue.text: Fat boy eating last of butter

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the word for boy surrounds the single letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the final letter of butter

explanation.surface: An overweight lad tucks into some butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking and baking.

clue.text: Rip-off artist finally duped novelist

parts.note: a con is a swindle or rip-off
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the final letter of duped

explanation.surface: A con artist has at last fooled a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rip-off artist' reads as one swindler, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad was the Polish-born British author of Heart of Darkness and Lord Jim.

clue.text: Celebration justifies tasty sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the letters sit inside the words around it

parts.note: found across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A party is a good excuse for delicious sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or holiday, especially a religious one in Spanish-speaking countries, a festive occasion.

clue.text: Devil with tail up is annual visitor

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving the tail up means the last letter is shifted higher, nearer the top

parts.note: Satan is the Devil

explanation.surface: The Devil, tail raised, turns up every year.
explanation.walkthrough: The final N of SATAN moves up two places; Satan and Santa share their letters, a well-known joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas comes once a year on Christmas Eve to deliver presents, a yearly caller.

clue.text: Gradually turning Volume Six into English

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the volume and six are placed within English

parts.note: Eng. is the abbreviation for English
VI is the Roman numeral six
vol. is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: Volume Six is slowly being translated into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolving means developing gradually over time, slowly changing into something else.

clue.text: Rope and ring in snout

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the ring goes within the snout

parts.note: a snout is a nose
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A farmer leads a bull by a rope and a ring through its nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot that tightens when pulled.

clue.text: Scotsman's continental skipping rope

indicators.note: skipping means passing over, so the letters of rope are left out

parts.note: a continental is a European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot from the mainland is jumping rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotsman's' is read as 'Scotsman is', the definition followed by the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Euan is a traditional Scottish boy's given name, so it can name a man from Scotland.

clue.text: Republican helping after president's lapse

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so the Republican and helping follow the president's name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A Republican aide's blunder after the president slipped up.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from what is normal or expected, a temporary slip in conduct or judgement.

clue.text: Great swimmer worried over extremes of climate in Canada

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the other pieces go within the abbreviation for Canada

parts.note: CAN is the abbreviation for Canada

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so only the first and last letters of climate are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of climate

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for worried is read backwards

parts.note: worry ate at him: to eat is to worry or trouble

explanation.surface: A champion swimmer frets about the harsh weather in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great swimmer' suggests an Olympic champion; it means a whale, great in size.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetaceans are the order of marine mammals including whales and dolphins, some of the largest animals in the sea.

clue.text: Badly rusted cleaning equipment

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters end up in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Some cleaning gear has corroded badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A duster is a cloth used for wiping dust off furniture and surfaces around the house.
